Documents from the reading list (summaries written by the lab; cite only these):
1. [ketcheson-2008] 2008: Highly efficient strong stability-preserving Runge-Kutta methods with low-storage implementations. SSP methods with many stages and low storage: the ten-stage fourth-order method with coefficient 6, and the family with n^2 stages of order 3 and coefficient n^2 - n built from Euler steps of size dt/(n^2 - n) and one convex combination, shown optimal among methods with that many stages. Results: SSPRK(10,4) with coefficient 6; SSPRK(n^2,3) with coefficient n^2 - n
2. [spiteri-ruuth-2002] 2002: A new class of optimal high-order strong-stability-preserving time discretization methods. SSP Runge-Kutta methods with more stages than their order have larger coefficients: the four-stage third-order method has coefficient 2 and the five-stage fourth-order method coefficient 1.508, both found by numerical optimization and both better per stage than the classical SSP methods. Results: SSPRK(4,3) with coefficient 2; SSPRK(5,4) with coefficient 1.508
3. [gottlieb-shu-1998] 1998: Total variation diminishing Runge-Kutta schemes. Proves that among two-stage second-order and three-stage third-order methods the Shu-Osher methods have the largest CFL coefficient (one), and that every four-stage fourth-order method needs a negative coefficient in its Shu-Osher form, so classical RK4 is not SSP without a downwind operator. Results: SSPRK(2,2) and SSPRK(3,3) are optimal with coefficient 1; no four-stage fourth-order explicit method has nonnegative Shu-Osher coefficients
4. [ruuth-2006] 2006: Global optimization of explicit strong-stability-preserving Runge-Kutta methods. A global optimization search for the largest SSP coefficients of explicit methods with given stages and order; confirms the earlier optimal methods and finds new ones for higher order, with the values treated as numerically optimal rather than proved. Results: numerically optimal SSP coefficients for explicit methods; 1.508 confirmed for SSPRK(5,4)
5. [shu-osher-1988] 1988: Efficient implementation of essentially non-oscillatory shock-capturing schemes. Writes Runge-Kutta methods as convex combinations of forward Euler steps so that any property forward Euler has under a CFL restriction (such as being TVD) carries over with the time step multiplied by the smallest ratio of the combination coefficients. Gives the two-stage second-order and three-stage third-order methods with coefficient one, now called SSPRK(2,2) and SSPRK(3,3). Results: the Shu-Osher form: convex combinations of Euler steps; the CFL coefficient as the minimum ratio alpha/beta; SSPRK(2,2) and SSPRK(3,3) with coefficient 1
6. [gottlieb-ketcheson-shu-2011] 2011: Strong Stability Preserving Runge-Kutta and Multistep Time Discretizations. The monograph on SSP methods: the theory through the radius of absolute monotonicity, the canonical Shu-Osher form, tables of optimal explicit and implicit methods and their coefficients. Results: tables of optimal SSP coefficients by stages and order
